hook_text: Double the size of a house drawing. Twice the paint? Nope, four times.
clip_script: The original rectangle covers four times six, twenty-four squares. The enlargement covers eight times twelve, ninety-six squares. That is four times as many, not twice as many. Both the length AND the width doubled, so the area is multiplied by two times two, four.
visual_style: A small house drawing on a grid zooms to double size; four copies of the small house tile inside the big one; paint tins multiply from one to four.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to draw enlargements and reductions on squared paper.
